title: Open direct image and the all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficient-change mate
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the topology of the extended $\ell$-adic absolute value, and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $B(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ on profinite sets, with all continuous maps, and $A_E(S)=C(S,E)$ for a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$ with its restricted norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $B_T=p_T^*B$ and $A_{E,T}=p_T^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The continuous inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ gives the coefficient map $A_{E,T}\to B_T$ by postcomposition and pullback [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Modules are internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open $k$-immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and fix one finite intermediate field $E$. Let $C\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_{E,U}})$ have bounded cohomology with finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Write $L_T=B_T\otimes^L_{A_{E,T}}-$ for derived coefficient extension [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] and $Rj_{*,A_E},Rj_{*,B}$ for the ordinary total right derived module direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. The canonical morphism
$$\beta_C:L_XRj_{*,A_E}C\longrightarrow Rj_{*,B}L_UC$$
is an isomorphism. Precisely, under $j_B^*\dashv Rj_{*,B}$ it is adjoint to
$$j_B^*L_XRj_{*,A_E}C\ \cong\ L_Uj_{A_E}^*Rj_{*,A_E}C\ \xrightarrow{L_U(\epsilon_C)}\ L_UC,$$
where $\epsilon$ is the $A_E$-coefficient counit and the displayed comparison is pullback/tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. All categories are ordinary ambient module derived categories; no completion of $\Omega$ or coefficient sheaf, and no filtered-union interpretation of $B$, is used. No constructibility conclusion about either side is part of this statement.

proof.text: Write $T$ for the scalar functors in the statement. For any $f$ define $\beta_f$ by exactly the displayed counit mate, not by choosing an isomorphism. The locus where $\beta_{j,C}$ is invertible is closed under shifts and triangles: restrict scalars from $B$ to $A_E$, which reflects isomorphisms and commutes with derived pushforward by lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction. On K-flat representatives the restricted scalar extension is $C\otimes^L_{A_E}B$, by lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction. Its stated formula $x\otimes a\mapsto a g(x)$ identifies the restricted counit mate, after tensor symmetry, with the projection morphism for $j$ and the fixed $A_{E,X}$-module $B_X$. Therefore lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift supplies exactness and compatibility with connecting arrows; lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three gives triangle closure. This argument uses no invertibility assertion for a projection formula.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent alteration/tame-boundary reduction; all-continuous coefficient version, step 1

proof.text: The same locus contains zero and is closed under finite sums, isomorphisms and retracts. For the last assertion write $F=T_XRj_{*,A_E}$, $H=Rj_{*,B}T_U$. If $C\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{r}C$ has $ri=1$ and $\beta_G$ is invertible, the inverse of $\beta_C$ is $F(r)\beta_G^{-1}H(i)$, by naturality and $ri=1$. Apply lem-sfb-tame-pair-proper-generators: it suffices to prove the assertion for $G=Rq_{*,A_E}K$, where $K=(b_!L)[0]$, $p:Y\to X$ and $q:V\to U$ are proper, $j':V\hookrightarrow Y$ is the inverse image of $j$, and $(Y,D,W,L)$ is the specified regular tame pair. Thus the extra geometric assumptions are imposed on generators, not on the given $C$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent alteration/tame-boundary reduction; all-continuous coefficient version, step 2

proof.text: For such a generator, finite-rank lisse $L$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_{E,W}^{r}$, so it has the finite constant scalar model $E^{r}$ on the trivial stratification. The schemes of the generator are Noetherian. The exact extension-by-zero assertion of lem-sfb-scalar-model-immersion-extension gives $K\in\Dbc(V,A_E)$. The finite-$E$ case, and only that case, of lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible gives $Rj'_{*,A_E}K\in\Dbc(Y,A_E)$. These are precisely the two bounded-constructible hypotheses needed below for the proper comparison input. No corresponding constructibility assertion for the all-continuous coefficient ring is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent alteration/tame-boundary reduction; all-continuous coefficient version, step 3

proof.text:
First, for any $f$ and a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms, the pullback/tensor comparison $f_B^*T_T\cong T_Zf_{A_E}^*$ used in the statement is represented by the ordinary sheaf map $f_B^*(B_T\otimes_{A_{E,T}}P)\to B_Z\otimes_{A_{E,Z}}f_{A_E}^*P$, which is the comparison $\chi_f$ of lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization; by that node it equals $\theta_f^{-1}$, so $\beta_f$ is exactly the mate of the square $\theta_f^{-1}$ along $f_{A_E}^*\dashv Rf_{*,A_E}$ and $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$. For composable $Z\xrightarrow{g}T\xrightarrow{f}S$, scalar/pullback coherence in lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization and adjunction-compatible composition in lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons allow mate-pasting, clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting. Applying its formula to the scalar/pullback squares gives
$$\beta_{fg,K}=Rf_{*,B}(\beta_{g,K})\circ\beta_{f,Rg_{*,A_E}K},$$
under the normalized derived-direct-image compositors. Indeed both sides are mates of the same composite inverse-image square; the counit of the composite is the composite counit specified in those nodes. Since $jq=pj'$, applying this identity twice yields
$$Rj_{*,B}(\beta_{q,K})\circ\beta_{j,Rq_{*,A_E}K}=Rp_{*,B}(\beta_{j',K})\circ\beta_{p,Rj'_{*,A_E}K}.$$
The two domains and codomains are identified using those adjunction-compatible compositors. This proves the equality for the canonical counit mate required by the item.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent alteration/tame-boundary reduction; all-continuous coefficient version, step 4

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-proper-scalar-comparison first to $p$ with input $Rj'_{*,A_E}K$, then to $q$ with input $K$; properness is part of the chosen generator and step 3 verified bounded constructibility. Both proper comparisons are isomorphisms. The map $\beta_{j',K}$ is an isomorphism by lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-tame-boundary-comparison: its regularity, strict normal crossings, selected outer components, and tame $L$ are exactly the generator data. Derived direct image preserves isomorphisms, so the right side of the equality in step 4 is invertible, and its left postcomposition $Rj_{*,B}(\beta_{q,K})$ is invertible. Consequently $\beta_{j,G}$ is invertible. Steps 1 and 2 and finite generation give invertibility for the original $C$, with the prescribed counit normalization.
